correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the parity action from the local Lagrange polynomials and independently checked the exact Fourier trace, determinant, Schur–Cohn residual and compensation identity with audit-support/simpson_symbol.py. For 0<d<1 the determinant modulus is at most 1−d+d²<1 and the residual is strictly positive off the constant block, where the two eigenvalues are 1 and 1−2d. Reflection and a commuting two-node translation transfer this to the second half of the Courant interval. At f=1 the cyclic permutation has a unique normalized invariant but no general convergence, consistent with the Finding. Simpson integration and subtracting the two parity weightings give the exact checkerboard extremum. Products preserve the Simpson row precisely when the ordered scalar equation holds; the given radical solves it with both displacements nonresonant. The supplied finite checker was inspected, not executed.

evidence: Lemma 3, PDF pp. 9–10, sets p=1−exp(iω) and normalizes the Schur residual by 16λ²(1−λ)², obtaining λ²(2−λ)|p|⁴/64, exactly the factorization in the Finding's proof after undoing the normalization. It explicitly concludes strict contraction for p≠0 and interior λ.

evidence: Sum equations (7)–(8) over elements: the off-diagonal entries of the resulting stochastic two-by-two matrix are d(2−d) and d². Their ratio immediately gives the stationary even weight d/2. Iteration discards all other modes by Lemma 3; subtract the elementary Simpson row to obtain the sharp bias (take parity-extreme data). Multiplying two of these same two-by-two matrices into the Simpson row gives exactly the ordered compensation polynomial.

value.rationale: The difference between reconstructed and conserved mass is physically motivated, and the formula is pedagogically useful. But the exact same prior stencil and strict contraction already dictate the entire fixed-grid classification; the two-step result is a single multiplication of the published zero-mode matrices, with no additional stability or useful smooth-grid conclusion. Under the scientific standard this is a mechanically implied exact invariant, not a surviving distinct contribution.
